analysis.title: Upstart Holdings (UPST): 3Q26 Key Takeaways: Macro headwinds lead to reduced volume outlook
key_insights: Shares closed +0.28% vs S&P +0.36% on 3 Nov after a weak run into the print. GS says the results and macro commentary were roughly in line with what bearish investors expected.
GS calls the macro commentary on the call fairly negative and expects it to weigh on the stock near term.

Management is pointing to margins on secured lending products not improving and possibly declining within the 0-25% band, with a pivot back to a growth strategy. GS says this could make the 4Q exit contribution margin a high-water mark into next year.
Management described benefits of the bank charter strategy, which GS views as fairly positive. Opex is coming in in line to slightly better than telegraphed.

GS sees risk/reward as fairly balanced: an improved margin profile against little visibility into 2027 originations and profitability and high sensitivity to the macro environment. The stock trades at 7x GS Q5-Q8 EPS estimates. GS stays Neutral and wants more visibility on the medium-term growth targets before turning more constructive.
3Q26 net revenue from fees was $364mn vs Visible Alpha consensus $342mn (7% ahead). Transaction volume was $4.12bn vs ~$4.14bn consensus, and take rate was ~8.8% vs 8.2% consensus.

3Q26 contribution profit was $218mn (60% margin) vs consensus $190mn (56% margin). Adjusted EBITDA was $89mn (24% margin) vs 22% consensus margin. EPS was $0.33 vs $0.22 consensus. Fixed operating expenses were +6% vs consensus.

FY26 revenue guidance was cut to roughly $1.35bn from $1.4bn. Revenue from Fees guidance was raised to $1.32bn from $1.3bn. The FY26 adjusted EBITDA margin guide fell to 19% from 21%, implying about $260mn vs $294mn prior. Management guided Q4 2026 opex flat sequentially.

October originations were about $1,249mn, or roughly $48.1mn per origination day. The Upstart Macro Index (UMI) rose to 1.53 from 1.49 in September, which GS reads as rising default rates. GS views the originations and UMI as negative for the stock.

GS's implied 4Q26 guide is revenue of $307mn vs $383mn consensus (-19.9%), revenue from fees of $331mn vs $358mn, net interest income of -$24mn vs +$25mn, and adjusted EBITDA of $53mn (17% margin) vs $92mn (24%) consensus.

GS cut its 12-month price target to $24 from $28, using about 8x Q5-Q8 adjusted EBITDA (about 11x before, on less visibility into the macro outlook). Rating is Neutral and the stock was $21.31 at the time of the report.

market_movers.rationale: PT cut to $24 from $28 on a lower multiple (~8x vs ~11x Q5-Q8 EBITDA) given less macro visibility and lower estimates. Implied upside is 12.6% and the rating stays Neutral.

risk_factors: Upside risks: better than expected credit, improved underwriting model updates, higher than expected loan-to-value ratios (LTVs).
Downside risks: worse than expected credit, higher competition, less favorable regulation, weaker new product adoption.
Macro uncertainty and limited visibility into 2027 originations and profitability.
Secured lending margins may not improve and could decline within the 0-25% band.

vol_and_positioning: UPST had been weak into the print and traded in line with the market after results (+0.28% vs S&P +0.36%). GS says the print matched what bearish investors were expecting.

tension_points.bull_case: The bank charter strategy has benefits, opex is in line to slightly better than telegraphed, and the improved margin profile leaves the stock at 7x GS Q5-Q8 EPS estimates.
tension_points.bear_case: Macro commentary was negative, secured lending margins may not improve and could decline within the 0-25% band, the 4Q exit contribution margin may be a high-water mark, and there is little visibility into 2027 originations.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS wants greater visibility on achieving the company's medium-term growth targets before getting more constructive.
